feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is stated for it. Evidence: iteration 1 (mass 0.6, score 114.4) is the reference, with oval progress 0.47, oval oscillation 0.28 and max_error 0.061 to 0.066 m. Iteration 9 (mass 0.8) lost score mainly on s-bend progress (0.26 to 0.16), so heavier mass hurts bends. Iteration 4 (mass 0.5 with a faster drivetrain) raised oscillation to 0.33 without a progress gain, so its lighter-mass signal is confounded. Iteration 8 (wheel_track 0.09) kept oval progress at 0.456 with oscillation 0.251, which suggests the narrower track can offset some of the extra jitter a lighter body brings. Integration point: I kept the iteration-1 controller unchanged, so the race measures mass alone and I have added no damping. Change the next design by what the race shows. If s-bend progress rises above 0.26 and oval progress holds near 0.47 with oscillation at or below about 0.3, try mass 0.4 kg next. If oscillation rises above about 0.33 without a progress gain, the lower mass is overshooting, so return to 0.6 kg and move to controller damping rather than geometry. If s-bend progress falls, the lower mass is not helping, so keep 0.6 kg.
requested_changes: If s-bend progress rises above 0.26 and oscillation stays at or below about 0.3 at mass 0.5 kg, set mass to 0.4 kg (lower bound 0.4) next. Iteration 9 showed that 0.8 kg cost bend progress (0.26 to 0.16), so the trend points toward lower inertia.

If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.33 at mass 0.5 kg without a progress gain, set mass back to 0.6 kg and wheel_track to 0.09 m. Iteration 8 showed that 0.09 m held oval progress (0.456) and cut oscillation to 0.251 relative to the 0.10 m reference.

Keep the five-sensor 12 mm layout at y 0.03 m (x -0.05 to +0.05). Iteration 5 (lead 0.02 m, score 91.8) and iteration 6 (lead 0.04 m, score 109.9) both fell below iteration 1 (114.4), and iterations 2 and 3 showed the 16 mm and 8 mm footprints did not help.
